battle.name: 凱撒入侵不列顛
battle.theater: 肯特郡海岸與泰晤士河下游
battle.brief: 前55年與前54年，凱撒兩度率羅馬軍團渡海打不列顛：頭一年登陸即遭戰車與林地逼退，幾星期後撤回高盧；第二年以五個軍團再渡海，擊敗卡圖維拉尼聯軍，逼卡西維拉努斯交出人質。卡面那身希臘重步兵裝備早已退場，但它留下的弧面大盾、重標槍與短劍，正是凱撒用來在英國海岸站穩陣腳的東西。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 交戰的兩方是羅馬共和國與不列顛東南部的部落聯盟。羅馬一方由執政官兼將軍蓋烏斯·尤利烏斯·凱撒統率，骨幹是公民兵團：前55年只帶第十三、第十四兩個軍團渡海，把拉比埃努斯與三個軍團、約一萬名羅馬士兵留在高盧；前54年傾全國之力，五個軍團加大量盟邦輔兵同時登船。輔助兵力包括高盧與日耳曼盟軍的騎兵、克里特與羅得島的弓兵，糧食與攻城所需全靠從高盧本土出發的運輸船隊。另一方不是國家而是聯盟：肯特郡的卡圖維拉尼人由卡西維拉努斯率領，特里諾萬特、凱尼馬尼、阿特里巴特各部各有首領，北方莫里尼人與梅納皮人同樣捲入，並且與高盧北部的部族往來密切，甚至有高盧騎兵渡海加入英方。可以確定的是，凱撒自稱渡海是為了阻止不列顛以高盧的兵源與騎兵增強自己、威脅高盧行省，而英軍沒有統一指揮，只在共同敵人面前鬆散協同；羅馬一方則是整個共和國的國家戰爭機器，一紙命令就能抽出五個軍團與數百艘船。戰線自登陸的肯特郡海岸起，向內陸推到泰晤士河下游，北面的高地從未被觸及。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Roman Republic and a confederation of tribes in south-eastern Britain. The Roman side was commanded by the consul and general Gaius Julius Caesar, with the citizen legions as its backbone: in 55 BC he took only the thirteenth and fourteenth legions across the water, leaving Labienus with three legions and some ten thousand Roman soldiers to hold Gaul; in 54 BC he mobilised the resources of the whole state, and five legions with a large body of allied auxiliaries embarked together. The auxiliaries included cavalry from the Gallic and German allies and archers from Crete and Rhodes, while food and every piece of siege equipment came from the transport fleet that sailed from the mainland of Gaul. The other side was not a state but a confederation: the Catuvellauni of Kent were led by Cassivellaunus, and the Trinovantes, the Cenimagni and the Atrebates each had their own chiefs; in the north the Morini and the Menapii were drawn in as well, and they kept close ties with the tribes of northern Gaul, with Gallic cavalry even crossing the sea to join the British. What is certain is that Caesar claimed to be crossing in order to stop Britain drawing on the man-power and the horse of Gaul to strengthen itself and threaten the Gallic province, while the British had no unified command and co-operated only loosely in the face of a common enemy; the Roman side was the war machine of an entire republic, able to extract five legions and several hundred ships on a single order. The front ran from the coast of Kent where the landings were made inland to the lower Thames, and the highlands to the north were never touched.
people: 貫穿兩次遠征、決定全部節奏的只有凱撒一人。前55年他以一次速戰速決的襲擊證明高盧已在自己手裡，卻始終不在海峽兩岸留常備兵；前54年他改用另一套辦法，先派騎兵巡邏威懾沿海部族，再以主力會戰逼卡西維拉努斯屈服，最後讓各部落分別交出人質。不列顛方面最重要的名字是卡西維拉努斯，凱撒稱他為卡圖維拉尼人的王：前54年他獨自率軍迎戰，在野地會戰中落敗，退過泰晤士河，最後交出騎兵與步兵為人質。曼杜布拉基烏斯原是特里諾萬特人的王，被卡西維拉努斯逐出，凱撒把他扶回王位，於是他成了羅馬在不列顛的代理人。康米烏斯原是阿特里巴特人的王、凱撒在高盧戰爭中的老盟友，前55年隨英軍出海，卻在戰場上被自己人重創，此後倒向英方。羅馬方面除凱撒外，第十三軍團的騎兵、克里特與羅得島的弓兵、高盧與日耳曼盟軍的騎兵，都在決定勝負的一擊中出手。凱撒在《高盧戰記》第五卷親筆記下這些人物與細節，這也是今天能重建兩次遠征的主要依據。
peopleEn: Only one man ran through both expeditions and set the tempo of everything: Caesar himself. In 55 BC he proved with a swift raid that Gaul was in his hands, yet he never left a permanent garrison on either shore of the channel; in 54 BC he changed his method, first sending cavalry patrols to overawe the coastal tribes, then bringing the main battle to bear so as to force Cassivellaunus to yield, and finally making each tribe hand over hostages separately. The most important name on the British side was Cassivellaunus, whom Caesar calls king of the Catuvellauni: in 54 BC he led the British alone, was beaten in the open field, withdrew across the Thames, and finally gave up cavalry and infantry as hostages. Mandubracius had been king of the Trinovantes before Cassivellaunus drove him out; Caesar put him back on his throne, and he became Rome's man in Britain. Commius had been king of the Atrebates and a long-standing ally of Caesar in the Gallic war; he crossed to Britain with the British in 55 BC, was badly hit by his own side in the fighting, and from then on leaned towards the British. On the Roman side, apart from Caesar, the cavalry of the thirteenth legion, the Cretan and Rhodian archers, and the Gallic and German allied horse all struck in the blow that decided the battle. Caesar wrote down these men and these details in the fifth book of his Commentaries on the Gallic War, and that is the principal evidence from which the two expeditions can be reconstructed today.
kits: 卡面是希臘重步兵：大方盾、雙手長矛、護腿、青銅頭盔，配一柄短劍。到了公元前55年，這個兵種本身早已退場：希臘城邦的方陣被馬其頓的長槍方陣吸收，希臘化世界裡的重裝步兵要麼被編入國王軍團，要麼淪為傭兵與雇傭兵的護衛；希臘式重裝裝備真正延續下來的地方，是被羅馬人吸收進公民兵團的標準配備。所以這件兵器在本役的位置是源頭件與對照件：凱撒的羅馬兵穿皮札甲、戴卡西亞式銅盔，手上是伊比利亞短劍與重標槍，背上是弧面橢圓大盾，腿上綁著長靴與護腿。那面大盾的弧形讓盾牌可以互相搭接，正是方陣「互相遮蔽」原則的遺存，但凱撒把它從密集方陣改成百人隊中各自為戰、彼此策應的散兵線——方陣的原理被拆散了用。英格蘭方面的裝備與之鮮明對照：長而可劈砍的鐵劍、小型圓盾與短矛，另有雙輪戰車；凱撒記下英軍作戰時把盾排列成互相扣連、前緣斜伸的蠻族式盾牆，並以戰車先行衝擊。攻城方面凱撒沒有帶攻城器械，第二次遠征在肯特郡一座沼澤邊的營地靠海運補糧；全役唯一一次工程作業，是用綁鐵鉤的原木在泰晤士河上架橋渡河。
kitsEn: The card shows a Greek hoplite: a large round shield, a two-handed spear, greaves and a bronze helmet, with a short sword at his side. By 55 BC the troop type itself had long since disappeared: the phalanx of the Greek city-states had been absorbed into the Macedonian sarissa phalanx, and heavy infantry in the Hellenistic world was either folded into the armies of the kings or reduced to mercenaries and their guards; the real continuation of the Greek heavy-infantry equipment lay in what the Romans absorbed into the standard kit of the citizen legions. So the weapon's place in this war is that of the source piece and the reference piece: Caesar's soldiers wore segmented armour and Casis-type bronze helmets, carried the Iberian short sword and the heavy pilum, bore a curved oval scutum on their backs, and strapped long boots and greaves to their legs. The curve of that scutum allowed shields to overlap against one another, the legacy of the phalanx principle that men cover each other, but Caesar broke the phalanx up into a line of fighting in which each century fought on its own while the others covered it — the principle taken apart and reused. The British equipment stood in sharp contrast: a long, chopping iron sword, a small round shield and short spears, together with two-wheeled chariots; Caesar recorded that the British closed their shields into a barbarian-style wall, locked one to another and slanted forward, and sent their chariots into the charge first. Caesar brought no siege engines; in the second expedition his camp in Kent beside a marsh was supplied with grain carried by sea, and the single piece of engineering work of the whole campaign was a bridge of logs bound with iron hooks thrown across the Thames.
tactics: 第一次登陸的戰術核心是「把登陸變成盾牆」：凱撒令士兵把大盾舉在頭頂與身前搭成遮蔽，抵住岸上的投射物與戰車撞擊，再以執旗手與百夫長為先跳入淺水強行開路；士兵在各船同時躍水登岸，才把灘頭變成陣地。登陸後的戰鬥發生在海邊與沼澤之間的狹窄林道，英軍藏身林邊，先以戰車衝擊，再以步兵投擲標槍；凱撒投入第三軍團騎兵與高盧盟軍騎兵，才把英軍逼回林中，隨後因天色、地形與追入林中的風險放棄追擊。第一次遠征實際上是一連串小規模接觸，沒有一場決定性會戰，凱撒在島上停留不到三星期便帶兵回高盧，只留少量高盧士兵守莫里尼人之地。前54年的打法完全不同：先以騎兵巡邏掃清海岸，再選海與沼澤夾峙、地勢狹窄但可設營的位置；因糧食不足，他從對岸「瓦魯斯」港運糧，並在船上儲備以備退路。主力會戰中，英軍以蠻族式盾牆步步推進，使羅馬兵一時難以砍劈；凱撒沒有硬壓，而是以克里特與羅得島弓兵的投射削弱敵前排，再令高盧、日耳曼與羅馬騎兵連續衝擊英軍兩翼與側後，英軍陣形一散即全線崩潰，戰車反而成了累贅。渡過泰晤士河後，凱撒用同樣思路處理政治：分割敵人、逐個部落單獨議和，最終讓各部族分別交出人質。
tacticsEn: The tactical heart of the first landing was the idea of turning the disembarkation itself into a shield wall: Caesar ordered his men to hold the great shields above and before their bodies as a roof against the missiles and the charge of the chariots, and then sent the standard-bearers and centurions in first to wade in and force a way; only when the soldiers leapt from the ships on every side at once was the beach turned into a position. The fighting that followed took place on a narrow track between the sea and a marsh, with the British hidden at the edge of the wood, striking first with their chariots and then throwing their spears; Caesar committed the cavalry of the third legion together with the Gallic allied horse, drove the British back into the trees, and then broke off the pursuit because of the light, the ground and the risk of following them into the wood. That first expedition was in fact a series of small contacts with no decisive pitched battle; after less than three weeks on the island Caesar sailed back to Gaul with his army, leaving only a few Gallic soldiers to guard the country of the Morini. The second expedition worked in a quite different way: cavalry patrols first swept the coast, then Caesar chose a site where sea and marsh closed in on a narrow strip on which a camp could be pitched; short of grain, he had it ferried over from the port he called Vara on the opposite shore, and stored it on the ships so that the army could fall back on it. In the main battle the British pressed forward behind their barbarian-style shield wall and for a moment the Roman soldiers could not get their swords to work; Caesar did not force the issue, but weakened the British front with the archers of Crete and Rhodes and then sent the Gallic, German and Roman cavalry in again and again against their flanks and rear, and the British line came apart at once, their chariots becoming a liability rather than an asset. After the crossing of the Thames Caesar applied the same logic to politics: divide the enemy, treat with each tribe separately, and in the end make each of them hand over hostages on its own.
data: 留下數字的只有凱撒自己的《高盧戰記》第五卷，而其中不少數字帶修辭性質。艦隊方面：前55年在莫里尼與維涅提一帶沿海徵集約八百艘船，另有烏比尼人交出的六十艘；前54年再度集結約八百艘，凱撒描述它們是從沿海各地徵來的船隻，連同高盧盟邦的船。兵力方面：前55年渡海只帶兩個軍團，兵員約一萬五千人上下，這是依凱撒敘述推得的量級，他沒有留下可核對的戰損；前54年為五個軍團，總兵力約四萬人上下（含盟軍輔兵），同樣是後世注釋家依文字推得，而非戰場清點。守方方面：卡西維拉努斯投降時交出的英軍人數，傳本記為約二千名騎兵與逾四千名步兵（或作交出此數為人質），各部族另交人質，其數沒有留下。時間上，兩次遠征都在夏季：前55年一次約在一個月內結束，凱撒在島上停留不足三星期；前54年自渡海到回師約兩個月。距離上，高盧莫里尼海岸的伊提奧斯港到不列顛南岸的海程不超過一百公里，凱撒記載船隊順風夜航、天亮前抵岸，航程僅數小時；由登陸地到泰晤士河約一百公里量級。全役沒有留下雙方確切的陣亡數字。
dataEn: The only numbers that survive come from the fifth book of Caesar's own Commentaries, and several of them are rhetorical in character. On the fleets: in 55 BC roughly eight hundred ships were gathered along the coasts of the Morini and the Veneti, with sixty more provided by the Ubini; in 54 BC a fleet of about eight hundred was assembled again, Caesar describing them as ships collected from every stretch of the coast together with those of the Gallic allies. On strength: in 55 BC only two legions crossed, with some fifteen thousand men in all — an order of magnitude inferred from Caesar's narrative, since he left no verifiable casualty figure; in 54 BC there were five legions and a total of about forty thousand men including auxiliaries, again an estimate drawn from the text by later commentators rather than a count made on the field. On the defender's side: the numbers Cassivellaunus gave up when he surrendered are recorded in the transmitted text as about two thousand horsemen and more than four thousand foot, or alternatively as that many being handed over as hostages; the tribes gave further hostages whose numbers are not recorded. On time: both expeditions fell in the summer. The first, in 55 BC, was over within about a month, Caesar spending less than three weeks on the island; the second, in 54 BC, lasted about two months from the crossing to the return. On distance: the passage from the port of Itius on the Morini coast of Gaul to the south coast of Britain is no more than a hundred kilometres, and Caesar records that the fleet sailed by night with a favourable wind and made the British coast before dawn, the crossing taking only a few hours; the march from the landing place to the Thames is on the order of a hundred kilometres. No exact casualty figures survive on either side for the campaign as a whole.
cause: 兩次遠征的起因都長在高盧的邊境上。凱撒前55年渡海時，高盧本土剛被壓平：前54年他平定了維涅提與貝爾加一帶的最後一波起義，宣稱高盧已平，並在接下來的冬天駐巴黎；然而高盧北部與不列顛之間往來密切，遠在意大利時就已有高盧人渡海遷居不列顛，前55年凱撒又聽到消息，說大批高盧騎兵已渡海加入不列顛的戰事，而沿海部族還在不斷招募。對凱撒而言，這是「敵人在境外集兵」的現實威脅：只要不列顛能持續吸走高盧的兵源與騎兵，高盧行省的邊境就永遠無法鞏固；而且元老院中反對他的派系指控他擅自用兵、浪費共和國的軍資，也是他必須用一場對外勝利來堵住悠悠眾口的理由。前55年那一次因此更像一次示警的襲擊：打得贏就撤走，讓不列顛各部族明白羅馬隨時能過海來。然而英軍並沒有被嚇退，反而在商船上向凱撒求援，於是前54年他改變計畫，傾全軍之力再來一次，目標不再是驚嚇，而是迫使各部族認下宗主權、繳出人質，把不列顛南部變成高盧行省的外圍。前54年他之所以敢傾全軍，也是因為前52年的全民抗戰與前51年阿萊克西亞之役已讓高盧本土沒有另一場大規模戰爭可以拖累他。
causeEn: The causes of both expeditions grew out of the frontier of Gaul. When Caesar crossed in 55 BC the tribes of Gaul had just been put down: in 54 BC he had crushed the last rising in the country of the Veneti and the Belgae, declared Gaul pacified and spent the following winter at Paris; yet the ties between northern Gaul and Britain were close, Gauls had already crossed the sea to settle in Britain even back in the time of the Italian wars, and in 55 BC Caesar learned that large numbers of Gallic cavalry had crossed to join the fighting in Britain while the coastal tribes went on recruiting. For Caesar this was the concrete danger of an enemy mustering beyond the frontier: for as long as Britain could keep draining away the man-power and the horse of Gaul, the frontier of the Gallic province could never be secured; and the faction in the senate opposed to him, which accused him of using armed force on his own authority and of squandering the military resources of the state, was a further reason for him to silence his critics with a victory abroad. The expedition of 55 BC was therefore in effect a warning raid: win, then withdraw, and let the tribes of Britain understand that Rome could come over the sea at any time. But the British were not cowed, and it was from a merchant vessel that they sent word to Caesar asking for help, so in 54 BC he changed his plan, brought the whole army back and came again, his object no longer to frighten but to force the tribes to acknowledge his overlordship and give up hostages, turning southern Britain into an outwork of the Gallic province. What allowed him to bring the whole army in 54 BC was that the general rising of 52 BC and the victory at Alesia in 51 BC had left no second large war in Gaul to hold him back.
impact: 對不列顛，這兩場戰爭是它第一次被羅馬有系統地打開的大門。凱撒沒有留下常駐軍隊與行省機構，卻用人質安排把英格蘭東南部的部落變成羅馬的附庸：卡西維拉努斯歸附，曼杜布拉基烏斯復位，北方莫里尼人與梅納皮人交出人質，貝爾加部族因懼怕英軍與高盧勾結而倒向羅馬。這種安排讓凱撒在前52年回師高盧、迎戰維欽托利時不必再擔心英軍從海峽另一端插手，把全軍得以投入阿萊克西亞的殲滅戰。對羅馬，這場勝利本身就是政治資本：高盧的戰利品、軍功與民眾支持，把凱撒從一個被指為過度使用武力的地方將領，推成共和國最有勢力的執政者，直接埋下前49年內戰的伏線。對英格蘭長遠而言，羅馬的錢幣、陶器與鐵器隨後大量流入南部沿海，東南部在往後兩百年裡逐漸形成受羅馬影響的精英階層；而凱撒《高盧戰記》第五卷又成為英國文獻中最早關於本土的紀錄，兩千多年後仍有學者逐字比對他寫下的地名與今日的考古遺址，試圖找出凱撒營地所在的位置。
impactEn: For Britain, these two wars were the first time the island was systematically opened up by Rome. Caesar left behind no permanent garrison and no provincial administration, but he turned the tribes of south-eastern Britain into dependents of Rome through an arrangement of hostages: Cassivellaunus submitted, Mandubracius was restored, the Morini and the Menapii in the north gave hostages, and the Belgae, frightened of any collusion between Britain and Gaul, turned towards Rome. That arrangement allowed Caesar, when he returned to Gaul in 52 BC to meet Vercingetorix, not to fear an intervention from the far side of the channel, and it let him commit the whole army to the decisive work at Alesia. For Rome the victory was itself political capital: the plunder of Gaul, the honours and the popular support turned Caesar from a provincial commander accused of using armed force without authority into the most powerful consul of the republic, and it laid the fuse for the civil war of 49 BC. In the longer term for England, Roman coinage, pottery and iron work poured into the southern coasts, and over the following two centuries a Romanised elite took shape in the south-east; while the fifth book of Caesar's Commentaries is the earliest surviving written record of the British Isles, and scholars are still matching his place names word by word against today's archaeological sites in an attempt to locate the camps he describes.
result: 結果是軍事上的成功與政治上的有限。前55年那次登陸，凱撒用登陸盾牆與騎兵反擊擊退英軍，但沒有佔領任何一座聚落、沒有取得人質、沒有留下常駐佔領，幾星期後就撤回高盧，只在莫里尼人之地留了少量高盧士兵駐守。可以確定的是這一趟確立了一個事實：英格蘭擋不住有備而來的羅馬軍團。前54年再來，情況完全不同。凱撒以五個軍團登陸肯特郡，逼卡西維拉努斯放棄泰晤士河以北的抵抗，攻下對方營地，英軍在步兵與戰車混編的正面壓力下被側翼騎兵擊潰；卡西維拉努斯最後交出人質，曼杜布拉基烏斯重獲王位，各部族分別與凱撒達成協議。最後凱撒帶著人質與俘虜回到海岸，以數百艘船返回高盧。留下來的東西有兩樣：一是不列顛南部各部族對羅馬宗主權的承認，二是「英國可以被征服」這個念頭——它由凱撒傳給後世，到公元43年克拉狄烏斯登陸時才真正實現。凱撒自己沒有完成的事，公元43年之後的羅馬皇帝和他的後繼者用另一套方式補上了；但要記住的是，凱撒的兩次遠征從來沒有帶著常駐軍與永久據點回去，他帶走的只有人質、承諾與傳聞，而凱撒《高盧戰記》第五卷把這個島寫成不列顛，這個名字從此成了它在歐洲書面上的稱呼。
resultEn: The result was a military success and a political one of limited scope. In the landing of 55 BC Caesar used the shield-covered disembarkation and a counter-charge of cavalry to drive the British back, but he occupied no settlement, took no hostages, left no permanent occupation, and within a few weeks withdrew to Gaul, keeping only a small body of Gallic soldiers to guard the country of the Morini. What the expedition did establish was one fact: Britain could not stand against a Roman army that came prepared. The second expedition of 54 BC was a different matter altogether. Caesar landed five legions in Kent, forced Cassivellaunus to give up resistance north of the Thames, stormed the British camp, and broke the British line with a flank charge of cavalry against the combined pressure of foot and chariots; Cassivellaunus finally gave hostages, Mandubracius was restored to his throne, and each tribe came to separate terms with Caesar. At the end Caesar took the hostages and the prisoners back to the coast and returned to Gaul with several hundred ships. Two things were left behind: the acknowledgement of Roman overlordship by the tribes of southern Britain, and the idea that Britain could be conquered — an idea passed on by Caesar to later generations and only actually realised when Claudius landed in AD 43. What Caesar did not achieve was taken up by the Roman emperors and their successors after AD 43, in a different form; but it should be remembered that neither of his expeditions ever went home with a permanent garrison or lasting bases, taking back nothing but hostages, promises and rumour, and that the name of the island in European writing was fixed by the fifth book of Caesar's Commentaries, which calls it Britain.
